pointers.sentence: `UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response`, which `cache_page` runs too, returns a response unstored at the first of its checks that holds, among them checks on the flag `FetchFromCacheMiddleware` leaves, streaming, a status other than 200 or 304 and a `"max-age"` of 0, and stores a 200 that passes them all unless its timeout is 0; the fixes of 2026 changed what it refuses and adds to `"Vary"` (`django/middleware/cache.py:UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response`).

`SessionMiddleware.process_response` now adds `"Cookie"` to `"Vary"` whenever it sets or deletes the cookie; standing inside `UpdateCacheMiddleware`, it hands on a response that sets a cookie and varies on `"Cookie"`, which is refused (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware.process_response`; [`SessionMiddleware`: the cookie and the save](../auth/session-middleware.md)).
`split_directive_names` lowers each name and drops its value, so `private="Set-Cookie"` counts as `"private"` (`django/utils/http.py:split_directive_names`).
`split_header_value` now strips every part it yields, and `has_vary_header` the name it is asked about (`django/utils/http.py:split_header_value`, `django/utils/cache.py:has_vary_header`).
`split_header_value` now strips every part it yields, and `has_vary_header` the name it is asked about (`django/utils/http.py:split_header_value`, `django/utils/cache.py:has_vary_header`).
It now varies on Authorization unless its Cache-Control has `"public"`, as RFC 9111's section 3.5 allows, the comment says (`django/middleware/cache.py:UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response`).

Under WSGI that is the server's affair; Daphne, the release notes say, ignores them too (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`; [Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md)).

`DomainNameValidator` refuses a value with a newline in it (CVE-2026-53878; 5.2.16, 6.0.7): its pattern ends at `"\Z"`, the string's end (`django/core/validators.py:DomainNameValidator.__init__`; [Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md)).

`DomainNameValidator` refuses a value with a newline in it (CVE-2026-53878; 5.2.16, 6.0.7): its pattern ends at `"\Z"`, the string's end (`django/core/validators.py:DomainNameValidator.__init__`; [Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md)).
The notes put the escaping in `log_response`, which calls it, as does the development server (`django/utils/log.py:log_message`; [Logging](../startup/logging.md)).

A user with an unusable password could still be told apart by timing (CVE-2024-39329; 5.0.7): `verify_password` now runs the default hasher once on random characters when the stored password is unusable, its hasher unknown or the password given `None` (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:verify_password`; [Password hashing: `make_password` and the hashers](../auth/hashers.md)).

The mod_wsgi handler's `check_password` let names be told apart by timing too (CVE-2025-13473; 5.2.11, 6.0.2), and now calls the same mitigation (`django/contrib/auth/handlers/modwsgi.py:check_password`).

`PasswordResetForm.send_mail` catches any exception from the send and logs it to `"django.contrib.auth"` (`django/contrib/auth/forms.py:PasswordResetForm.send_mail`; [Password reset: `PasswordResetTokenGenerator` and the reset views](../auth/password-reset.md)).

`Storage.save` checks a name with `validate_file_name` on arrival, after `Storage.get_available_name` and after `_save`: a subclass that overrode `Storage.generate_filename` without its checks could save outside its directory, though Django's own could not (CVE-2024-39330; 5.0.7) (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage.save`; [File storage: `Storage`, `FileSystemStorage` and `storages`](../services/storage.md)).

`extract`, which startproject and startapp use for a template given as an archive, refuses a member unless `os.path.commonpath` of its path and the target is the target: a path into a sibling directory whose name began with the target's passed before (CVE-2025-59682; 5.1.13, 5.2.7) (`django/utils/archive.py:BaseArchive.target_filename`; [Paths and archives: `safe_join`, `safe_makedirs` and `extract`](../utils/paths.md)).

They used to change the process's umask for a moment, which in a threaded server could reach another thread's files and directories (CVE-2026-25674; 5.2.12, 6.0.3) (`django/utils/_os.py:makedirs`, `django/core/cache/backends/filebased.py:FileBasedCache._createdir`).

They used to change the process's umask for a moment, which in a threaded server could reach another thread's files and directories (CVE-2026-25674; 5.2.12, 6.0.3) (`django/utils/_os.py:makedirs`, `django/core/cache/backends/filebased.py:FileBasedCache._createdir`).

`GenericInlineModelAdmin.get_formset` gives its forms a `BaseForm.has_changed` that answers false for an existing row the user may not change and, since this fix, for a new row they may not add, as `InlineModelAdmin.get_formset` does, so the formset never saves it (CVE-2026-4277; 5.2.13, 6.0.4) (`django/contrib/contenttypes/admin.py:GenericInlineModelAdmin.get_formset`; [Inlines: `InlineModelAdmin` and its formsets](../admin/inlines.md)).

The change list's formset for `ModelAdmin.list_editable` could create rows; `ModelAdmin._save_formset` raises `BadRequest` for a changed form whose object is new (CVE-2026-4292; 5.2.13, 6.0.4) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._save_formset`; [The change list's columns: `list_display` and `list_editable`](../admin/list-display.md)).
The field's own validators, the comment says, may allow such schemes (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:display_for_field`).

The salt now carries a prefix and the given salt's length (`django/core/signing.py:_cookie_signer_salt`); [What changed in security: Content Security Policy and signing](security.md) tells it, with `SIGNED_COOKIE_LEGACY_SALT_FALLBACK`, which when true reads cookies signed the old way.

`EmailBackend.open` now holds a new connection aside until STARTTLS and the login have succeeded, makes it the backend's connection only then, and closes what a failed attempt left at its next call or in `EmailBackend.close` (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.open`; [Sending email: `mailers` and the email backends](../services/mailers.md)).

`GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value` raises `DisallowedRasterLookup`, a `SuspiciousOperation`, for a dictionary, a string or a path, and `BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value` tries a string only as a geometry, refusing it when `GEOSGeometry` cannot read it; a value wrapped in a `GDALRaster` passes, and assigning to a field is unchanged (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value`, `django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value`; [Spatial fields: the geometry fields and `RasterField`](../contrib/spatial-fields.md)).

`GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value` raises `DisallowedRasterLookup`, a `SuspiciousOperation`, for a dictionary, a string or a path, and `BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value` tries a string only as a geometry, refusing it when `GEOSGeometry` cannot read it; a value wrapped in a `GDALRaster` passes, and assigning to a field is unchanged (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value`, `django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value`; [Spatial fields: the geometry fields and `RasterField`](../contrib/spatial-fields.md)).

A `GDALRaster` made from bytes now gives its in-memory file the bytes' length, so `GDALRaster.vsi_buffer` reads back exactly them; it could read some 32 bytes past the buffer (CVE-2026-53877; 5.2.16, 6.0.7) (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.__init__`, `tests/gis_tests/gdal_tests/test_raster.py:GDALRasterTests.test_vsi_buffer_length`).
